summary: Parses one key=value configuration line from the buffer starting at offset 0xC of the parsing context. Strips a trailing carriage return, trims leading whitespace (space 32 / tab 9), stores the location of the '=' separator at offset 0x30C (this[195]), and lowercases the key side. Returns 0 on a parsed line, 1 for a blank/whitespace/comment line, and 2 on a line that fails the start-token check or is empty.

operations.description: Compute the length of the line buffer at offset 0xC with strlen and write a null terminator at its end.
If the last content character is a carriage return (13), replace it with a null terminator.
Copy the line buffer (offset 0xC) into a local scratch buffer, stopping at the terminating null.
Scan past leading whitespace in the copied line: skip characters that are space (32) or tab (9).
sub_588640 compares the trimmed line start against the delimiter set at unk_5C30B8; if it does not match, return 2 as a format error.
If the line is now empty after trimming, return 2.
A trailing character of space (32) or closing brace (125) classifies the line as a comment and returns 1.
sub_587C20 locates the '=' separator position inside the line buffer.
Store the located '=' separator pointer at this[195] (offset 0x30C) and clear the found character.
Lowercase the key side character by character via sub_589A35 until the '=' (61) separator is reached.
Return 0 on a successfully tokenized line, 1 on a blank/comment line, 2 on a format error.

unresolved: Exact semantics of unk_5C30B8 delimiter/quote set used by sub_588640 and sub_587C20 are unknown.
sub_587C20, sub_588640 and sub_589A35 are only known by their call sites here; their standalone behavior is unverified.
Whether offset 0x30C (the '=' pointer) is consumed by the caller LineReaderFromBuffer after this returns is unproven.
Owner object of the parsing context is unknown.
